title: Why Halle Berry and Anna Paquin are missing from Doomsday
excerpt:
Storm and Rogue are absent from the announced Doomsday ensemble.
A report on the Russo brothers' comments examines the film's narrative-driven casting.
body_md:
The return of several performers from the original X-Men films is one of the major attractions of Avengers: Doomsday. Yet the announced ensemble has also prompted questions about familiar faces who have not been included. Halle Berry and Anna Paquin, known for playing Storm and Rogue, are among the most conspicuous examples.

A report discussing comments from directors Joe and Anthony Russo examines how the filmmakers assemble the cast of their crossover. The available feed excerpt emphasizes their approach to selecting characters according to narrative requirements, but it does not reproduce their complete answers about Berry or Paquin. Consequently, it cannot establish a specific confirmed reason for either performer's absence.

The Russos previously directed Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame, both of which featured extensive ensembles. Those films distributed their characters across different storylines and gave them varying degrees of prominence. Managing that balance is a significant challenge for any production involving numerous established protagonists.

Doomsday is particularly notable for bringing together performers associated with the Marvel Cinematic Universe and actors whose superhero films preceded it. James Marsden's return as Cyclops recalls the original cinematic X-Men team, introduced in 2000. Against that background, the absence of Storm, Rogue and Iceman from the currently familiar lineup is especially noticeable to longtime viewers.

Berry portrayed Ororo Munroe, the mutant capable of manipulating weather conditions, in the earlier films. Paquin played Rogue, whose powers involve absorbing the abilities and energy of others. Both characters occupy important places in the history of the cinematic franchise, making their potential involvement a subject of understandable interest.

The crossover also carries historical significance for Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige. Early in his producing career, Feige worked as an associate producer on the original X-Men film after being recruited by Lauren Shuler Donner. He now oversees a cinematic universe capable of bringing those earlier interpretations of Marvel characters into contact with newer ones.

From an editorial perspective, the challenge is not simply to assemble the largest possible cast, but to give the returning characters meaningful functions within the story. The available report does not reveal how those functions have been assigned in the completed film.

Absence from an announced cast or promotional campaign does not independently confirm or rule out an undisclosed appearance. Nor does the available material establish whether negotiations occurred with either actor. Avengers: Doomsday is scheduled for theatrical release on December 18, 2026. Until more information is disclosed, the precise reasons for the missing characters remain unconfirmed.
